Quantification

A missing precursor usually means it was too faint to detect, not that it was absent at random. limpa turns that into a model in two steps. dpc() fits one detection probability curve for the whole experiment: the chance a precursor is detected, given how abundant it is. dpcQuant() then gives every protein a value and a standard error in every biopsy, using its observed precursors and, through the curve, what its missing ones imply. Nothing is filled in as if measured; a value resting on few detections carries a wide standard error, and later fits weight it less.

After quantification this step builds the blood index, removes contaminant proteins and keeps proteins detected often enough to compare.

Packages

library(here)
library(limma)
library(limpa)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
source(here("00_Setup", "Shared_functions", "workbooks.R"))
step <- here("01_Processing", "02_Quantification")
inputs <- c(
  precursors = "01_Processing/01_Precursors/c_data/precursors.rds",
  contaminants = "01_Processing/02_Quantification/references/contaminants.csv"
)
paths <- vapply(inputs, here, character(1))
stopifnot(file.exists(paths))

Input

The precursor matrix from 01_Precursors: log2 intensities, NA where undetected, one column per biopsy.

y <- readRDS(paths[["precursors"]])
c(precursors = nrow(y), proteins = n_distinct(y$genes$Protein.Group), biopsies = ncol(y))
precursors   proteins   biopsies 
     22342       2401         48

Detection probability curve

The curve is logistic: P(detected | log2 intensity y) = plogis(β0 + β1 y). The slope β1 says how strongly detection depends on abundance; 0 would mean values go missing at random. limpa’s authors report slopes of about 0.7 to 1 in real data. The curve is fitted on every precursor, contaminants included, because it describes the instrument’s detection of any precursor.

dpcest <- dpc(y)
dpcest$dpc
     beta0      beta1 
-11.948040   0.679028 
plotDPC(dpcest)

Quantify proteins

dpcQuant() fits each protein’s precursors together (protein level plus a fixed offset per precursor), with the missing ones entering through the curve and a prior estimated from all proteins. It returns complete log2 values in E, a standard error per value in other$standard.error, and per protein the precursor count (NPrec) and the share of values observed (PropObs).

proteins <- dpcQuant(y, "Protein.Group", dpc = dpcest)
c(proteins = nrow(proteins), biopsies = ncol(proteins), missing = sum(is.na(proteins$E)))
proteins biopsies  missing 
    2401       48        0

How much each protein rests on: precursors per protein and the share of its values observed.

proteins$genes |>
  as_tibble() |>
  summarise(
    proteins = n(), one_precursor = sum(NPrec == 1), median_precursors = median(NPrec),
    median_observed = round(median(PropObs), 2), observed_under_half = sum(PropObs < 0.5)
  )
# A tibble: 1 × 5
  proteins one_precursor median_precursors median_observed observed_under_half
     <int>         <int>             <dbl>           <dbl>               <int>
1     2401           390                 4            0.54                1078
quantile(proteins$other$standard.error, c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1))
       0%       25%       50%       75%      100% 
0.0224522 0.3267140 0.5056006 0.7440418 1.6458513

Standard errors grow as fewer values are observed:

tibble(
  observed = proteins$genes$PropObs,
  se = apply(proteins$other$standard.error, 1, median)
) |>
  ggplot(aes(observed, se)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.6, alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(x = "share of values observed", y = "median standard error") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10)

Samples

plotMDSUsingSEs() (limpa) places biopsies by their protein values, like limma’s plotMDS, but takes the standard errors into account. Colour is time point, label the biopsy.

tp_colour <- c(T1 = "#1B9E77", T2 = "#D95F02", T3 = "#7570B3")
mds <- plotMDSUsingSEs(
  proteins,
  labels = colnames(proteins), col = tp_colour[proteins$targets$timepoint], cex = 0.7
)
round(mds$var.explained[1:2], 3)
[1] 0.318 0.141

Blood index

Blood in a biopsy dilutes the muscle proteins. The index is each biopsy’s mean log2 HBB and HBA1, taken from limpa’s complete values, centred on the mean biopsy. Comparisons carry it as a covariate.

blood_rows <- grepl("(^|;)(HBB|HBA1)(;|$)", proteins$genes$Genes)
proteins$genes[blood_rows, c("Genes", "NPrec", "PropObs")]
       Genes NPrec   PropObs
P68871   HBB    38 0.6524123
P69905  HBA1    27 0.7368827
stopifnot(sum(blood_rows) >= 2)
blood <- colMeans(proteins$E[blood_rows, , drop = FALSE])
proteins$targets$blood <- unname(blood - mean(blood))
blood_index <- proteins$targets |>
  as_tibble() |>
  select(sample_id, subject, group, timepoint, blood)
summary(blood_index$blood)
   Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
-2.1601 -0.6658 -0.2446  0.0000  0.5995  2.6823 
ggplot(blood_index, aes(timepoint, blood, colour = group)) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.15, seed = 1)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "blood index (centred log2)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10)

Contaminants

references/contaminants.csv holds the 222 contaminant proteins the earlier protein-level pipeline resolved (plasma, immunoglobulin, erythrocyte, keratin, complement, globin, leukocyte; see references/README.md). They are removed now, after quantification: each protein is quantified from its own precursors, so removing them afterwards leaves every other protein’s values unchanged apart from the shared prior.

contaminants <- readr::read_csv(paths[["contaminants"]], show_col_types = FALSE)
removed <- contaminants |>
  filter(uniprot_id %in% rownames(proteins)) |>
  arrange(class, gene)
count(removed, class)
# A tibble: 7 × 2
  class              n
  <chr>          <int>
1 complement        12
2 erythrocyte       19
3 globin             7
4 immunoglobulin    41
5 keratin           18
6 leukocyte          5
7 plasma           120
c(on_list = nrow(contaminants), present = nrow(removed))
on_list present 
    222     222 
proteins <- proteins[!rownames(proteins) %in% contaminants$uniprot_id, ]
nrow(proteins)
[1] 2179

Proteins not on the list cannot be removed by it. Remaining keratin, immunoglobulin and haemoglobin genes, printed for review and kept:

review <- proteins$genes |>
  as_tibble(rownames = "uniprot_id") |>
  filter(grepl("(^|;)(KRT|IG[HKL]|HB[ABDGQ])", Genes)) |>
  select(uniprot_id, gene = Genes, n_precursors = NPrec, prop_observed = PropObs)
review
# A tibble: 1 × 4
  uniprot_id gene  n_precursors prop_observed
  <chr>      <chr>        <dbl>         <dbl>
1 P08727     KRT19            3         0.208

Detection filter

filterByDetection() (limpa) keeps proteins with at least one observed precursor in at least n.samples biopsies. Its help page suggests the smallest group size for a small study; each group-by-time cell holds 8 biopsies, so a kept protein was detected in at least one cell’s worth of biopsies (decisions log, 2026-10-15). It runs after quantification, as limpa intends: the curve and the prior use every precursor.

detected <- filterByDetection(proteins, n.samples = 8)
table(kept = detected)
kept
FALSE  TRUE 
  120  2059 
dropped <- proteins$genes[!detected, ] |>
  as_tibble(rownames = "uniprot_id") |>
  select(uniprot_id, gene = Genes, n_precursors = NPrec, prop_observed = PropObs)
proteins <- proteins[detected, ]
c(proteins = nrow(proteins), one_precursor = sum(proteins$genes$NPrec == 1))
     proteins one_precursor 
         2059           276

Protein values per biopsy

The same check as for precursors, now on limpa’s complete protein values: one curve per biopsy, which should overlap.

plotDensities(proteins, legend = FALSE, main = "")
round(summary(apply(proteins$E, 2, median)), 2)
   Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
  16.33   17.65   17.81   17.75   17.89   18.19

Validation

stopifnot(
  !anyNA(proteins$E), all(proteins$other$standard.error > 0),
  identical(colnames(proteins), proteins$targets$sample_id),
  !any(rownames(proteins) %in% contaminants$uniprot_id), !anyNA(proteins$targets$blood)
)

Summary

2059 proteins in 48 biopsies, after removing 222 contaminants and 120 proteins detected in fewer than 8 biopsies. The detection curve’s slope is 0.68; 276 kept proteins rest on a single precursor.

Save

quantification.rds is limpa’s EList: E, other$standard.error, genes and targets with the blood index. dpcDE() in the comparisons reads it directly.

out <- file.path(step, "c_data")
dir.create(out, showWarnings = FALSE)
saveRDS(proteins, file.path(out, "quantification.rds"))
write_workbook(
  list(
    dpc = tibble(term = names(dpcest$dpc), estimate = unname(dpcest$dpc)),
    proteins = as_tibble(proteins$genes, rownames = "uniprot_id") |>
      select(
        uniprot_id, protein_name = Protein.Names, gene = Genes, n_precursors = NPrec,
        prop_observed = PropObs
      ),
    blood_index = blood_index,
    contaminants_removed = removed,
    contaminant_review = review,
    detection_dropped = dropped
  ),
  c(
    "Detection probability curve: intercept (beta0) and slope (beta1).",
    "Every protein kept: names, precursor count and share of values observed.",
    "Blood index per biopsy (centred mean log2 HBB and HBA1).",
    "Contaminant proteins removed, with class and reason.",
    "Keratin, immunoglobulin and haemoglobin genes not on the list, kept for review.",
    "Proteins detected in fewer than 8 biopsies, dropped by filterByDetection()."
  ),
  file.path(out, "quantification.xlsx"), inputs, paths
)
